An ad-free GUI with a rebuilt full-height download graph that stays correct at gigabit speeds, a dark theme that reliably comes up on a fresh install, and a rebranded banner.

## Changed

- **New README banner wordmark.** "JDownloader" is now set in Bree Serif — our house wordmark font (as on BombVault / ShipLog) — instead of the generic Arial Black, so the banner reads as our brand. Claim set in Lato, the shared claim font across all repos.
- **Ad-free by default.** JDownloader's built-in advertisements are now switched off out of the box: the bottom **"Become premium user" banner** (which filled the tab row below the download graph), the **premium-alert** column nags, the status-bar **"+ premium"** button, and the **special-deal** popups. Only advertisements are touched — the Donate button and every functional setting are left exactly as you set them. The flags live in `org.jdownloader.settings.GraphicalUserInterfaceSettings` (e.g. `bannerenabled`); they are re-applied on each start so a JDownloader self-update can't quietly bring the ads back.
- **Hardened bootstrap download.** The first-start download of `JDownloader.jar` is retried (3×) and validated as a real jar (a captive portal or DNS hijack serving an HTML page no longer ends up saved as the launcher). If all attempts fail, the log shows a loud, repeating error banner instead of exiting silently to an empty desktop.
- **Dialog agent hardening.** Dialog auto-confirm has per-window click guards (no rapid re-clicking), and the agent's state markers are wiped on every container boot *and* before every JD launch, so a crash-looping JD can't inherit stale "theme applied" state. Any JD dialog the agent doesn't recognise is logged once with its verbatim title and text — so if JDownloader ever introduces another forced dialog, the container log carries exactly the strings needed to fix it, instead of a guess from a screenshot.

## Fixed

- **Download graph: doubled in height, and rebuilt so it stays correct at any speed.** JDownloader hardcodes the toolbar row that holds the speed graph to 32px, with no config key — with the ads disabled, that corner looked cramped and half-empty. The bundled GUI agent now raises that row to 64px at runtime (tool buttons stay centered, and the tweak survives JD's toolbar rebuilds and self-updates). Doubling the height also surfaced a real bug in JDownloader's graph painting (AppWork `Graph`): every sample is plotted as `(int)(height * value * 0.9) / max` with `value` in raw bytes/s — the `height * value` product is a 32-bit multiplication that overflows above ~34 MiB/s at the 64px row this image uses (~67 MiB/s even at JD's stock 32px). Overflowed samples wrap low or clip away entirely, and the speed-limit line vanishes (only its red text stays). The agent therefore hides the native speed meter and paints its own graph with 64-bit arithmetic: **full height at any speed**, same look (theme colours, average overlay, speed-limit band, localized texts). The native panel stays alive underneath, so its speed-limit menu keeps working (clicks are forwarded). The log prints `[jd-dialog-agent] replaced the speed graph (native math overflows above ~34 MiB/s)` once active.
- **Speed-limit field clipped long values.** The speed-limit field in the *Settings* menu had a fixed width sized to fit only "500.00 KB/s" (JDownloader hardcodes it in `MenuEditor.getEditorWidth()`), so a higher limit such as "10,216 MiB/s" was cut off and unreadable. The bundled GUI agent now relaxes that fixed width and grows the menu so the whole value, including its unit, is shown.
- **White GUI after a clean install.** JDownloader shows a "you have changed the look and feel to FlatLaf Dark — restart to apply" dialog on some fresh installs. The container's dialog agent didn't recognise that dialog, so it sat there unanswered: JD kept running with the default light look-and-feel (a white GUI) even though the dark theme was fully installed. The agent now confirms that dialog — matched on its text (locale-tolerant), answered with the restart-affirming button — and JD restarts itself once into the full dark theme. If the dialog ever appears with button labels the agent doesn't know, it asks the container for one polite JD restart instead of leaving the GUI stuck, and logs the dialog's exact title and text so it can be matched precisely in the next release. (Deliberate side effect: manually changing the look-and-feel in the GUI now also triggers the restart that applies it.)
- **The READY banner could lie.** It used to fire once JD's API port was up and the patched FlatLaf jar existed on disk — which says nothing about whether the theme was actually *applied* (in the white-GUI bug above, the banner fired while the GUI was white). The agent now records the actually-active look-and-feel, and `JDOWNLOADER IS READY` only prints when the expected theme is genuinely applied. If that can't be verified within ~10 minutes, the log says so honestly (`JDOWNLOADER IS UP (theme NOT verified)`) with a pointer to the relevant log lines, instead of printing the same READY banner.
- **CI hygiene.** The icon asset workflow no longer runs (and fails) on tag pushes.
